analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.

analysis.evidence: Lot chooses כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, “the whole plain of the Jordan.” The river name identifies which plain he chooses.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes the proper noun יַרְדֵּן and doubles its initial yod.

analysis.evidence: Lot chooses the Jordan plain, then וַיִּסַּע לוֹט narrates his departure. The following וַיִּפָּרְדוּ describes Lot and Abram parting.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject. The initial נ of נסע assimilates to ס, marked by the dagesh.
